etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French adulte, from Latin adultus (“grown up”), perfect passive participle of adolescō (“I grow up”). Compare adolescent.

definitions.definition: A fully grown human or other animal.

quote.citation: 1840, Georges Cuvier, Edward Blyth, Robert Mudie, George Johnston, J.O. Westwood, “The fourth order of reptiles—The batrachians”, in Cuvier's Animal Kingdom‎[1], page 286:
quote.text: The young not only differs from the adult by the presence of its gills, but its feet are only developed by degrees, and in several genera there are also a deciduous beak and tail, and intestines of a different form

definitions.definition: A person who has reached the legal age of majority.

quote.citation: 1837, Michael Donovan, Domestic Economy: Human Food, Animal and Vegetable‎[2], page 86:
quote.text: The paws of the adult brown bear, and also their hams, especially when smoked, are considered a great delicacy.

definitions.definition: Containing situations or discussions intended primarily for adults, such as serious crime, illicit drug use, extramarital affairs, etc.
(of a beverage) Containing alcohol, intended for consumption only by adults.
(of a cookie, gummy, etc.) Containing marijuana, intended for consumption only by adults.
Containing material of an explicit sexual nature; pornographic.
Containing excessive vulgar or profane speech, text or images, intended only for adults.
Intended for or restricted to adults rather than children due to size, maturity, knowledge level, judgement, etc.

quote.citation: 1973, Marshall Kaplan, Gans, and Kahn, Children and the urban environment (page 21)
quote.text: In May 1967 the WGBH Education Division submitted an initial proposal to HUD for a series of four adult television documentaries on conservation in an urban environment.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, slang) To behave like an adult.
(nonstandard, rare) To (cause to) be or become an adult.

quote.citation: 1974, Occasional Papers, numbers 42-46, Syracuse University, page 5:
quote.text: Womanhood was achieved at twenty-one, when the female was "adulted"; manhood was fully achieved at twenty-five,  […]

quote.citation: 2013, Ewa Rewers, The Contradictions of Urban Art, →ISBN, page 84:
quote.text: The process of adulting children […]  overlaps with the process of the uncontrolled infiltration of the media […]  into children’s imagination.
